open_risks.text: Five criteria can only be proven on the owner's devices: 16.24 (phone screens read as phone-native, S24 Ultra and Note 10+), 16.35 (Meadow frame timing with three glass layers, reported not bounded), 16.54 (onboarding swipe, scene, roots, stake and tours feel like the prototype), 16.61 (icon on the launcher and in the Dock), 16.62 (glass and petals under Impeller; widget tests render with Skia).

The phone Meadow stacks up to three BackdropFilter blurs (header, dock or pop-over, tab bar) over the animated scene; on the Note 10+ (Impeller on OpenGL ES) this is the costliest case and may drop frames. The owner chose real blur everywhere with cost reported, so a regression shows up only in review on the device.

Wave 2's tasks name interfaces wave 1 creates (GlassSurface and GlassTone in lib/design/glass, PhoneSheet and showPhoneSheet, StreakPill with fixed count, numberOnly and highlighted, the toast lift registration in lib/design/feedback/toast.dart, the onboarding title-top constant). If a wave 1 Lane named or shaped any of these differently, wave 2 Workers will build against names that do not exist; audit wave2.items.json against mitosis/proto-phone-shell before launching.

docs/specs/ is git-ignored and the new prototype under docs/prototype/ is uncommitted, while the tracked docs/prototype/project/ copies are deleted in the owner's working tree. Workers read the spec, decisions, icon and prototype only by absolute path from the main checkout; moving, deleting or committing over those files mid-run takes the reference away.

The approved spec section 17 has 12 assumptions; 1 to 11 were approved at read-back and 12 (Android system back keeps going back one onboarding step) with the written spec. The record and decisions file carry the full set.
At concurrency 2 with a 6-hour Worker timeout, wave 1 (12 Lanes) and wave 2 (8 Lanes, Meadow a 6-Step serial Lane) will each take many hours.

The new rose launcher icon is fully opaque, and reminder notifications use @mipmap/ic_launcher as their Android status-bar icon (lib/features/reminders/local_notifications_reminder_scheduler.dart:21). Android draws a status-bar icon as a white silhouette of its alpha, so reminders will probably show a plain white circle or squircle where the Flutter-logo outline used to be. Not checked on a device. The fix is a separate white-on-transparent peony notification drawable, which is outside the approved spec and needs the owner's call.

Light theme contrast on the new phone calendar: the accentInk terracotta (#c76a54) that the task and prototype name measures 2.98:1 for the 12-point 'This month' pill on paper glass and 3.28:1 for the 13-point 'Back to this month' on cardWarm (Flutter textContrastGuideline at 384x832), below WCAG AA's 4.5:1. Dark theme passes. The sweep has no contrast rule, so no test fails. The owner decides whether to keep the prototype colour or use a darker ink for small text.
